nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Long summer light drives the growth of reeds, water plants and algae in the shallow lakes and channels.

nodes.name: Danube floodwater
nodes.desc: The river splits into three main branches and spreads over a very low, flat plain, keeping the lakes, channels and reed beds flooded.

nodes.name: River silt & nutrients
nodes.desc: The Danube carries sediment and nutrients into the delta. Upstream dams have cut the sediment supply.

nodes.name: Bacteria, fungi & invertebrates
nodes.desc: Break down dead reed, plant litter and carcasses and return nutrients to the water and mud.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: Dominant grass of the delta marshes, forming vast reed beds. It grows in shallow water and tolerates brackish conditions. Birds such as pelicans nest in reedy vegetation.

nodes.name: White water-lily
nodes.desc: Floating-leaved plant of the still channels and lakes. Muskrats and mute swans are recorded eating it.

nodes.name: White willow
nodes.desc: Tree of the wet river levees and floodplain, rooted in the seasonally flooded ground.

nodes.name: Algae & phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae in the lakes and channels, nourished by river nutrients; the base of the open-water food chain.

nodes.name: Muskrat
nodes.desc: A semi-aquatic rodent, one of the more recent arrivals to the delta. It feeds on water-lilies and other marsh plants.

nodes.name: Mute swan
nodes.desc: Large waterbird that grazes on water plants, including water-lily and waterweed, in shallow wetlands.

nodes.name: Common carp
nodes.desc: Bottom-feeding fish of warm, slow water. In Europe it is a favoured prey of the great white pelican.

nodes.name: Non-biting midges
nodes.desc: Midge larvae live in the mud and water of the delta and are eaten by dragonflies, damselflies, fish and frogs.

nodes.name: Golden jackal
nodes.desc: Opportunistic canid recorded around the delta. GloBI records link it to muskrat, marsh frog, mute swan and wild boar.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: Omnivore of the reed and forest edges, recorded eating frogs and other small animals among many foods.

nodes.name: Marsh frog
nodes.desc: A large water frog of the channels and marshes, and prey for many birds, snakes and mammals in the delta.

nodes.name: Northern pike
nodes.desc: Ambush predator of weedy shallows. Adults eat mainly fish and frogs.

nodes.name: Eurasian otter
nodes.desc: Eats mainly fish, adding amphibians and other prey; it needs clean water with plenty of prey.

nodes.name: Pygmy cormorant
nodes.desc: A fish-eating bird nesting in reeds and willows. The delta holds the largest colony of the species.

nodes.name: Great white pelican
nodes.desc: More than half of Eurasian breeding great white pelicans nest in the delta. They fish cooperatively in shallows, taking carp in Europe.

nodes.name: Dalmatian pelican
nodes.desc: Nests on islands or in dense reeds in the delta. It swallows fish whole, including carp and pike.

nodes.name: White-tailed eagle
nodes.desc: Takes fish, waterbirds and carrion, and sometimes steals food from other fish-eaters.

nodes.name: Beluga sturgeon
nodes.desc: Giant migratory fish that runs up the Danube to spawn. Adults eat mainly large fish; it is critically endangered.
